passage:
A tourist followed an online map to a famous temple. The map led him to a narrow road behind the temple instead of the main gate.
He was frustrated until a local shop owner helped him. She said many visitors had made the same mistake. The temple had reported the error, but it had not been fixed yet.
The tourist took photos and sent a correction through the map app.
A month later, he received a message saying the route had been updated.
The mistake taught him that digital maps are not perfect objects. They are living systems, improved by many people. Users are not only followers; sometimes they are helpers.
